notes: Subject insert. q3 ('is the Nowell Codex the only surviving manuscript?') is determinate 'no' since 2026-10-31 (FINDINGS A1): the Ostrevane Codex is a second manuscript, distinct from the Nowell Codex (every entity is distinct), so the negation of the closed claim follows. The worlds differ only on the count (q2, fol, arithmetic), so they carry no axioms; w1 is no longer an exception. The Grendel bridge uses a relation (the work in which a monster attacks a king's hall). 2026-10-31 (justify.py): q3's 'no' is built from the edit and new_ms ('A medieval manuscript first found in 2025 is a different manuscript from the Nowell Codex.', its bridge, a firm fact: the new item is newly found, so not the known one); 'Beowulf survives in a single medieval manuscript, the Nowell Codex.' is q3's revision fact (the uniqueness belief that gives way; the answer never uses it).

bridge_refs.new_ms: A medieval manuscript first found in 2025 is a different manuscript from the Nowell Codex.

revision_refs.nowell_beowulf: Beowulf survives in a single medieval manuscript, the Nowell Codex.

queries.not_checked: fol (arithmetic): counts the members of a collection

fol.notes: Manuscripts are an uninterpreted sort; being a surviving medieval manuscript of Beowulf is a belief (manuscript_of, uninterpreted). w1 stores the count as a figure (number_of_members, ATTRIBUTES.md), which the insert does not recompute; w2 stores the counting rule over the stored list (an entry counts only if it differs from the earlier ones, so the new member's distinctness enters the count). Counting needs a closed world: every member the model knows is one of the named constants (presupposition named_only; Z3 does not need it to fix the value). The new member's distinctness from the stored one is part of the edit ('newly found').

nowell_beowulf.says: The manuscripts of Beowulf: the Nowell Codex. (stored, as a list)

named_only.says: Every surviving manuscript of Beowulf the model knows of is one of the named ones. (closed world)
named_only.z3: ForAll(x, Implies(manuscript_of(x, beowulf), Or(x == nowell, x == ostrevane)))

stores: number_of_members(beowulf_manuscripts) == count(manuscript_of(nowell, beowulf), And(manuscript_of(ostrevane, beowulf), nowell != ostrevane))
